title.narrative: Strengthening Access to Life-Saving Gender–Based Violence Services for Newly Arrived Sudanese Refugees and Affected Host Communities in Egypt

description.narrative: Overall this project aims to enhance the provision of accessible, confidential, and survivor-centred gender-based violence (GBV) prevention and response services. It aims to target newly arrived refugee women and girls of their reproductive age from Sudan as well as those from the host community in Egypt. Specifically, this project aims to provide life-saving GBV services with a focus on Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) and access to sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) for survivors of GBV and women and girls at-risk through 7 Women and Girls Safe Spaces (WGSS), 5 in Greater Cairo and 2 in Aswan. The WGSS will serve as an the entry point for life-saving activities including the provision of MHPSS support for GBV survivors, such as individual counselling and group-based sessions, temporary and emergency housing support for survivors and women at risk of GBV, cash assistance under GBV case management for survivors and women and girls at-risk of GBV, distribution of Dignity Kits for women and girls. The cash assistance is specifically targeting survivors and women and girls at-risk of GBV regardless of their registration status. This bridges the gap and complement with UNHCR’s Multipurpose Cash Assistance for registered refugees and asylum seekers. In addition to the provision of services through WGSS, the project will facilitate refresher training for the clinical management of rape (CMR) to frontline health service providers and provide medical equipment and supplies for safe delivery targeting survivors and women at-risk of GBV. This project aims to reach a total of 8,000 people (6,500 women and 1,500 girls), including 7,850 refugees and 150 host community members.
